outcomes.text: Find the full subject before deciding whether to contract a form of be.
Distinguish coordinated noun phrases from coordinated clauses.
Explain why contractions are possible in some sentences that contain and.

key_terms.definition: A reduced form written with an apostrophe, as in you’re for you are.
One subject made up of coordinated expressions, as in Maya and you.
The shortening of a form such as are to ’re and its attachment to the preceding word.

options.text: you
options.feedback: The one predicate applies to the entire coordinated subject.

options.text: you are
options.feedback: The one predicate applies to the entire coordinated subject.

options.text: Maya and you
options.feedback: The one predicate applies to the entire coordinated subject.

opening.prompt: Which words form the subject in “Maya and you are on the list”?

options.text: Two predicates with the same subject
options.feedback: Each side has a subject and its own predicate.

options.text: Two clauses
options.feedback: Each side has a subject and its own predicate.

options.text: Two pronouns in one subject
options.feedback: Each side has a subject and its own predicate.

opening.prompt: What does and join in “I’m at the desk, and you’re at the door”?

options.text: After the break, you are next.
options.feedback: You is the full subject only in the first wording. In the other two it is part of Jo and you.

options.text: Jo and you are next.
options.feedback: You is the full subject only in the first wording. In the other two it is part of Jo and you.

options.text: I think Jo and you are next.
options.feedback: You is the full subject only in the first wording. In the other two it is part of Jo and you.

opening.prompt: In which line can you reduce “you are” to “you’re” without reorganising the clause?

options.text: Sam waved, and you were near the exit.
options.feedback: Sam and you is a coordinated subject of the single predicate were near the exit.

options.text: Sam was near the exit, and you were there too.
options.feedback: Sam and you is a coordinated subject of the single predicate were near the exit.

options.text: Sam and you were near the exit.
options.feedback: Sam and you is a coordinated subject of the single predicate were near the exit.

opening.prompt: Which version keeps one shared predicate for Sam and the listener?

options.text: at ready after Lea
options.feedback: Lea is ready is already a complete clause. The second clause starts with its own subject, you.

options.text: at too
options.feedback: Lea is ready is already a complete clause. The second clause starts with its own subject, you.

options.text: at you’re
options.feedback: Lea is ready is already a complete clause. The second clause starts with its own subject, you.

opening.prompt: In “Lea is ready, and you’re ready too”, where does the second clause begin?

options.text: Tess and you’re both on duty.
options.feedback: The full are can follow Tess and you and begin the shared predicate.

options.text: Tess and you are on duty.
options.feedback: The full are can follow Tess and you and begin the shared predicate.

options.text: Tess is on duty, and you’re on duty.
options.feedback: The full are can follow Tess and you and begin the shared predicate.

closing.prompt: A volunteer writes “Tess and you’re on duty”, meaning Tess and the reader have the same assignment. Which repair keeps a single clause?

options.text: the usher
options.feedback: The relevant subject is inside the clause after that, and it includes both pronouns.

options.text: I and you
options.feedback: The relevant subject is inside the clause after that, and it includes both pronouns.

options.text: you alone
options.feedback: The relevant subject is inside the clause after that, and it includes both pronouns.

closing.prompt: In “The usher says that I and you are on the list”, what controls are?

options.text: The list names Jo and you’re.
options.feedback: In the first example, Jo checked the door already has a predicate. You is the full subject after and.

options.text: Jo and you’re checking the window.
options.feedback: In the first example, Jo checked the door already has a predicate. You is the full subject after and.

options.text: Jo checked the door, and you’re checking the window.
options.feedback: In the first example, Jo checked the door already has a predicate. You is the full subject after and.

closing.prompt: Which example has a valid contraction after and because a new clause starts there?

options.text: Are is chosen only because we is the nearest word.
options.feedback: One shared predicate tells us something about both parts of the subject.

options.text: Are follows the coordinated subject she and we.
options.feedback: One shared predicate tells us something about both parts of the subject.

options.text: We are the only people described as ready.
options.feedback: One shared predicate tells us something about both parts of the subject.

closing.prompt: Which explanation fits “She and we are ready”?

options.text: The second coordinates two subjects of leaving.
options.feedback: In the second example Kim has the predicate is staying, while you has are leaving.

options.text: The first coordinates noun phrases and the second coordinates clauses.
options.feedback: In the second example Kim has the predicate is staying, while you has are leaving.

options.text: Both coordinate clauses.
options.feedback: In the second example Kim has the predicate is staying, while you has are leaving.

closing.prompt: How do “Kim and you are leaving” and “Kim is staying, and you’re leaving” differ?
